Kerendia is the branded medicine labelled to reduce cardiovascular death and heart failure events in adults with heart failure with LVEF of 40% or above (openFDA label, effective 2025-08-28) since 2025-07-11 (NDA215341 efficacy supplement 9, book supplements table), so it matches on disease, pool, prescriber and payer. Case for higher: the class comparator, Camzyos, is $73,021.68 a Part D beneficiary in 2025 (572,709,028.53 over 7,843, same file), priced for obstructive HCM, a rare disease with a REMS and echocardiographic monitoring. A myosin inhibitor labelled in a pool of millions would not carry a rare-disease price, but a narrow hyperdynamic HFpEF label could sit well above Kerendia

column11: JUDGEMENT. No Phase 3 is registered. AURORA-HFpEF (NCT06122779) completes 2026-12-14 estimated, and the BMS Q2 2026 deck (8-K 0000014272-26-000018) lists AURORA data in 2026, so a Phase 3 starts in 2027 at the earliest. Analogue: FINEARTS-HF (NCT04435626), the outcomes trial that gave Kerendia its HFpEF label, started 2020-09-14 and completed 2024-05-15, and the label came on 2025-07-11 (NDA215341 supplement 9, book supplements table), so the first full year on sale, 2026, came six calendar years after the Phase 3 start. 2027 plus six is 2033
column12: BMS places MYK-224 HFpEF among potential launches in 2029 and beyond (JPM 2026 deck, 8-K 0001140361-26-000929, slide 7), which this sits inside. Case for earlier: a symptom or exercise-capacity endpoint, the route the myosin inhibitors took in obstructive HCM, is shorter than an event-driven outcomes trial; no HFpEF drug has been labelled on one. Case for later: AURORA is a safety study, so a dose-finding efficacy study may come before any Phase 3
